item.title: AI Agents and Agentic AI in Medicine: An Autonomy-Centred Scoping Review and Research Agenda
item.description: Abstract Artificial intelligence agents—software systems that perceive, reason, plan and act over multiple steps with limited human intervention—are moving from research prototypes towards clinical deployment. Recent reviews map what has been built; this one asks what would have to hold for such systems to be deployed safely. item.title: Comment and Control: Hijacking Agentic Workflows via Context-Grounded Evolution
item.description: Automation platforms such as GitHub Actions and n8n are increasingly adopting so-called agentic workflows, which integrate Large Language Model (LLM) agents for tasks such as code review and data synchronization. item.title: What makes an LLM a tutor? A component-centric survey of LLM-based and agentic tutoring systems
item.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are reshaping intelligent tutoring systems (ITSs) by reducing authoring costs and enabling flexible interaction. However, effective tutoring requires more than fluent responses. It also depends on pedagogical control, domain grounding, learner modeling, interaction design, orchestration, and reliable evaluation. item.title: PBFuzz: Agentic Directed Fuzzing for PoV Generation
item.description: PBFuzz: Agentic Directed Fuzzing for PoV Generation Artifact for the CCS 2026 paper. PBFuzz is a directed fuzzer that uses an LLM agent to generate property-based test inputs targeting specific bug locations. Given a bug ID and static call-graph analysis, the agent iteratively synthesizes Python input generators, executes the target under Magma canary instrumentation, and uses GDB/LLDB feedback to guide generation toward triggering the bug. item.description: Large multimodal model powered GUI agents are emerging as high-privilege operators on mobile platforms, entrusted to perceive screen content and inject inputs across application boundaries. item.description: Agent skills package reusable workflows and task-specific procedures into deployable natural-language artifacts for LLM agents. item.description: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. item.title: Can TDD improve the quality of LLM-migrated code? : A pilot study in an industrial context
item.description: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLM) has created new possibilities for automating software development, yet ensuring the quality of AI-generated code remains a major challenge.
